$comment: Machine-readable record of the request the apps send to OUR relay (decisions/0002), and the single place the multipart field names live. Both sides read this file: the Worker (worker/src/app.ts imports it and rejects any part it does not name) and the Android app (copied into assets at build time by android/app/build.gradle.kts, and the app constructs the request from it). It speaks our vocabulary only: the field keys are the wire names, no city display name, type or summary string appears anywhere in this file, because those belong to worker/src/adapters/reykjavik.ts alone (AGENTS.md). Where this file must agree with a city fact (the description limit, the accepted photo MIME types), it restates the fact with its source and scripts/check-relay-contract.mjs fails if the two files drift. Re-verify with: node scripts/check-relay-contract.mjs, which CI also runs.
source: decisions/0002 (the apps post to our relay, never to the city) and the repository's own request contract, established the day the app and the relay were first pointed at each other and disagreed on every field

endpoint.notes: the apps reach this on the relay's host, which is per build type and lives in BuildConfig.RELAY_BASE_URL on Android and BorgarlandCore.RelayEndpoint on iOS, never as a literal at the call site: the deployed https host for a release, and 127.0.0.1:8787 via adb reverse for development. The city is never on this path. The relay stores a report arriving on this path as a dry run ALWAYS and forwards nothing from it, whatever is configured (decision 0017): the city is reached only by an operator promoting a stored report, behind a credential no app holds.

reportId.format: 32 lowercase hex characters, generated by the app
reportId.notes: which report this IS, so sending it twice cannot file it twice. The relay stores it as the row's own id and answers a repeat with the row it already has, at 200 rather than 201. Optional because a build that predates it must keep working, and because the relay generates one when the app sends none — but an app WITHOUT it cannot be protected from a double press (#85, #88). It is not a secret and identifies nothing but the report: it is random per report, never derived from a device, and never reused.

category.notes: the only identifier the app has for a category. The relay's adapter derives the city's type, display name and summary from the slug; the app must not send them.

latitude.format: WGS84 decimal degrees, dot separator, e.g. 64.14658919
latitude.notes: full words, not the city's abbreviations: the short forms are the city's own field names for the same values (data/reykjavik-form.json fields.lat and fields.lng) and belong to the adapter alone.

longitude.format: WGS84 decimal degrees, dot separator, e.g. -21.93279823
longitude.notes: full words, not the city's abbreviation; see latitude.

description.notes: the relay appends the nearest registered address line for the crew (AGENTS.md) and drops it rather than overflow the limit; the limit is the city's, enforced by the relay.

email.notes:
the only way the reporter hears back: the city answers a report by email and by nothing else (data/reykjavik-form.json fields.email), so a report filed without one lands in the queue and the person who filed it is never told anything by anyone but us. Required BY US, exactly as the coordinate is (#163) — the city enforces neither.

Read `required` here as the APP's obligation, not the relay's tolerance. The Worker uses this file for the unknown-field allowlist alone and hardcodes the email as optional (worker/src/app.ts), so it keeps accepting a report from a build that predates this. That divergence is deliberate and is the only one: tightening the relay first would reject every report from builds 6 and 7, which are on testers' phones and send no email. The relay follows once no such build remains.

The address belongs to the phone rather than to the report. It is typed once, stored on the device beside the queue and the follow-ups, and prefilled — so a queued report picks up whatever address the phone holds when it finally sends, not the one it held when it was filed.

photo.notes: the app sends one today; the relay accepts repeated photo parts. The city calls these parts by another name; ours is photo, and it is the only name the app may write.
